ranked.headline: Learned models unify single-cell identity, annotation, integration and imputation tasks
ranked.summary: Deep generative, contrastive, and interpretable models are now applied across single-cell annotation, integration, and imputation tasks.

ranked.headline: Graph and probabilistic models integrate incomplete spatial multi-omics across platforms
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend spatial multi-omics integration to incomplete, cross-platform, and foundation-model-based tissue analysis.

ranked.headline: Chromatin measurements as inputs to models of regulatory activity
ranked.summary: Multimodal single-cell atlases and new normalization and reference methods are expanding chromatin-based inference of regulatory outcomes.

ranked.headline: Single-cell computational methods infer cell states, lineages, and disease targets
ranked.summary: Large single-cell atlases and multiomic resources now support data-driven design, trajectory inference, and target ranking across tissues and cell types.

ranked.headline: Biomolecular language model representations repurposed through new readout and…
ranked.summary: Learned protein and genome model representations are being redesigned at encoding and readout stages for tasks beyond their original pretraining objectives.

ranked.headline: Transformers and CNNs model DNA sequence and chromatin determinants of gene regulation
ranked.summary: Multiple February 2026 preprints and papers extend deep sequence and foundation models to CRISPRi perturbation, TF binding, and expression prediction.

ranked.headline: Bias-aware quantification and model-based inference reshape noncoding RNA measurement
ranked.summary: Recent work tests circRNA detection artifacts, sncRNA ligation bias, and model-based regulatory inference, making measurement choices central.

ranked.headline: Reference-free and graph-based tools advance pathogen genome typing and phylogenetics
ranked.summary: Recent work corrects sequencing and amplicon-induced errors and benchmarks reference-free typing across pathogen genomics workflows.

ranked.headline: Network structure links to transitions, oscillations and coordination in regulation
ranked.summary: Dynamical and network-based models now link regulatory topology to cell-state transitions, early-warning indicators and emergent homeostasis.

ranked.headline: Learned representations drive generative molecule and protein design across modalities
ranked.summary: Early 2026 preprints apply learned latent spaces to synthesizable, macrocyclic, and transcriptomics-conditioned molecular generation, protein backbone design,…

ranked.headline: Generative models target protein dynamics, receptor-ligand motion and antibody design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple generative sampling to dynamical trajectories and property-aware objectives, moving beyond static structure generation.

ranked.headline: Long-read and graph-based tools reconstruct and characterize microbial genomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications pair long-read assembly workflows with graph and text-aligned methods, alongside benchmarks of resistance-gene detection.

ranked.headline: Computational methods integrate single-cell, spatial and metabolic omics data
ranked.summary: Recent tools integrate single-cell, spatial, metabolomic and chromatin datasets, extending multi-omics analysis beyond transcriptomic layers.

ranked.headline: LLM agents and knowledge graphs add explicit constraints to molecular drug design
ranked.summary: Recent work couples LLM reasoning, grammar-constrained encoders, and knowledge graphs with pharmacological criteria for molecule optimization and repurposing.

ranked.headline: Single-cell CRISPR screens and deep learning decode regulatory elements and splicing
ranked.summary: Single-cell perturbation and sequence-based prediction now resolve regulatory elements and splicing at cell-type and nucleotide resolution.

ranked.headline: Simulations resolve transient conformational and interaction states controlling function
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply MD, Brownian dynamics and integrative restraints to capture short-lived disordered and condensate states.

ranked.headline: Latent-variable models resolve haplotype, multitrait and regulatory structure in genomes
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend probabilistic inference to haplotype typing, trans-eQTL mapping and multitrait fine-mapping.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-resolved polyploid genome assembly and allele-aware analysis tools
ranked.summary: Recent long-read, Hi-C, and graph-based methods now resolve haplotypes in autopolyploid potato and mixed-ploidy sugarcane.

ranked.headline: Network priors guide regularized feature selection and integration across omics layers
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs network priors with penalized, factorized, and robust selection methods for high-dimensional multiomic data.

ranked.headline: Evaluation design now drives reported accuracy in biological prediction models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints audit leakage, benchmark antimicrobial peptide regression and test saliency validity, exposing inflated or unvalidated performance claims.

ranked.headline: Scalable phylogenetic and pangenome methods with reproducibility and cost constraints
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers address scaling limits in phylogenetic network estimation, pangenome MUM finding, and parallel tree inference.

ranked.headline: Learned representations predict protein-ligand affinity and protein self-interaction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report 26x and 185x speedups for binding and structural-similarity prediction using coarse or distilled learned representations.

ranked.headline: Computational models link DNA methylation to aging, cancer, and tumor subtyping
ranked.summary: Recent studies pair methylation and single-cell or cell-free DNA data with computational models to resolve aging, tumor heterogeneity, and tumor detection.

ranked.headline: Software tools package regulatory simulation, metabolic modeling, and genome visualization
ranked.summary: Reusable packages now embed analysis steps directly into conda-forge, Galaxy, Jupyter, and web environments for routine reuse.

ranked.headline: Open Models and Benchmarks Extend Biomolecular Structure Prediction
ranked.summary: Open structure predictors and standardized datasets for RNA, antibodies, and peptides are now being benchmarked against established baselines.

ranked.headline: Learned representations link gene programs and expression to drug response prediction
ranked.summary: February 2026 preprints pair learned encoders with gene-program, expression, and multi-modal priors for perturbation and drug prediction.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and distributed pipelines advance single-cell RNA-seq analysis tooling
ranked.summary: Arbitrarily large scRNA-seq datasets and evaluation of AI agents on single-cell tasks motivate scalable, verifiable analysis tools now appearing as preprints.

ranked.headline: Software tools advance variant classification, GWAS meta-analysis, and cfDNA profiling
ranked.summary: Five February 2026 publications introduce or benchmark tools for reproducibility and scale across variant, GWAS, and cfDNA analyses.

ranked.headline: Computational and proteomic methods map ligand, TCR, and kinase substrate recognition
ranked.summary: Structure-informed simulation, design, and proteomic readouts are now applied to receptor, TCR, kinase, and drug-binding recognition problems.

ranked.headline: Software maps PTMs, coevolving residues and Mg2+ ions onto sequence and structure data
ranked.summary: Four software papers from early February 2026 add evolutionary and structural context to residue-level sequence, modification, and ion-binding data.

ranked.headline: Structural variation and transposable elements shape genome evolution across lineages
ranked.summary: Chromosome-level and pangenome datasets are now resolving transposon activity, inversions and archaic insertions within and across species.

ranked.headline: In silico prediction of missense and synonymous variant functional impact
ranked.summary: Structure-aware and synonymous-site predictors now extend computational pathogenicity assessment beyond canonical missense variants.

ranked.headline: Mapping non-SNV variation from single-cell mosaicism to biobank CNVs and oligogenic risk
ranked.summary: Single-cell, biobank-scale and multi-ancestry studies now resolve STR, CNV and digenic variation beyond SNVs in human genomes.

ranked.headline: Spectrum-level computation links MS/MS structures, similarity and conjugated metabolites
ranked.summary: Reverse search of 1.32 billion public MS/MS spectra and cross-polarity similarity learning are reported together in February 2026 preprints and papers.

ranked.headline: Modeling metal coordination, kinase reorganization, and induced fit in ligand binding
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a Bioinformatics paper apply receptor flexibility and metal coordination to binding-site prediction, selectivity, and ligand design.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomics maps conserved RNA structures and regulons across microbial taxa
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply cross-genome comparison to deep-sea genes, bacterial regulons, cyanobacterial RNA structures, and gut phages.

ranked.headline: New statistical methods improve detection across proteomic and omics datasets
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers refine aggregation, categorization, and dimension reduction to improve detection in noisy omics data.

ranked.headline: Evolutionary models of proteins, pangenomes and tumors tested against data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test explicit evolutionary and progression models for proteins, bacterial pangenomes, and tumors against large or real datasets.

ranked.headline: Databases and pipelines expand RNA virus, Cas9 PAM, and endogenous retrovirus annotation
ranked.summary: Reference resources now enable detection of RNA viruses, Cas9 PAM preferences, and HERV protein domains.

ranked.headline: Harmonized, FAIR-compliant metadata and databases for public omics data
ranked.summary: Public omics repositories need standardized, machine-readable metadata, and three new resources address harmonization and FAIR-compliant reuse.
